Fach.et: From Middle High German vach, from Old High German fah, from Proto-West Germanic *fak, from Proto-Germanic *faką.

s: fan (handheld device used to induce airflow, especially in order to cool oneself)
Fächer.et: 15th century, from fachen (“to stoke, stir up fire”) + -er. The verb is derived from Latin focō. The noun might also be a direct borrowing from Latin focārius (“he who stokes the hearth fire”), but this is unlikely.

Fackel.et: Inherited from Middle High German vackel, from Old High German faccala, fackala, fackila, fackula, fackla, from Proto-West Germanic *fakkulā (“torch”).

s: not understandable (for technical terminology or words)

-fach.et: From Middle High German vach (“-fold”), from Proto-Germanic *faką (“division, interval”).

s: medical specialist (male or of unspecified gender)
IT specialist, computer scientist (male or of unspecified gender)
